result.rationale:
In app/models/topic_embed.rb the diff adds `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "`. The url is interpolated directly into an anchor tag without any HTML escaping, and these posts are stored with cook_method raw_html (Post.cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts), so the raw string is rendered verbatim. A url containing a single quote (e.g. from an RSS item link or a user-supplied embed_url fetched via TopicRetriever) breaks out of the href attribute and enables HTML/attribute injection into the post content.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}` interpolates `url` directly into a single-quoted `href` attribute. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the attribute. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and later rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, this enables HTML/attribute injection (XSS) from feed-supplied URLs.
